messages:
kevin: Quick sync — thinking about a clean handover between central autoscaler and the pool operator for telemetry-driven actions. TL;DR: operator should make short-window tail-latency/prewarm decisions; central should keep longer horizon capacity planning and cost smoothing. does this boundary make sense? :thinking:
maria: makes sense in principle. what signals exactly are we passing at the boundary? cardinality concerns if every pool emits lots of histograms every 10s
ajay: +1 to the split. we should keep the contract small: basically an intent object, e.g. target_concurrency/rps, prewarm_count, ttl, priority_tag. small JSON blob, idempotent, with a reason string.
sophie: also need accounting: who gets billed for prewarm tokens? central needs to know or we'll double-count. and we need a TTL so operator doesn't hold forever.
dave: risk: operator prewarms then central immediately scales down nodes for cost reasons -> flapping. we need a lease/commit handshake. operator asks for prewarm, central returns either grant or suggest-alternative (reduced count).
kevin: agreed. proposal sketch of the contract (yaml):
```yaml
ScaleIntent: 
  pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-42
  requested_prewarms: 4
  target_rps: 120
  ttl_seconds: 90
  reason: "99th-latency > 300ms over 30s"
  idempotency_key: "uuid..."
```
central should reply with a grant: {granted_prewarms: n, expires_at, lease_id, notes} and operator must be resilient if grant < requested.
maria: for telemetry — use percentiles windows: short window 30s/1m for operator (99th, p99.9), longer 5-15m windows for central trending. sample rate: keep high-resolution histograms locally, but report aggregates to central to save cardinality.
ajay: implementation detail: use ring-buffered histogram at operator side + summarise into compact TDigest/ HDR buckets when sending intent. also tag intent with deploy-version to avoid warmup for canary model mismatches.
sophie: +1 on tagging. Also add a cheap proof-of-life metric for each granted prewarm so central can reclaim unused grants after grace. e.g., operator must ACK prewarm within 30s or central reduces credit.
dave: debugging: we need a single trace id across intent/grant; logs should show intent-id and lease-id. Example log: 
[pool-42] intent=abc123 req=4 grant=2 lease=lease-789 status=prewarm-ack
orch-bot: deployment: autoscaler v3.2 rolled out to us-west yesterday 03:12 UTC (canary 10% pools) :white_check_mark:
kevin: operational concerns: race conditions, idempotency, eventual consistency. operator should never assume immediate node availability; prewarm is best-effort. also expose telemetry counters for "intent_rejected_reason" to central alerts.
maria: SLO interactions: operator-handled prewarms should aim to protect p99 under the short-window SLO. central should prefer smoothing decisions to maintain cost targets. define an SLO handoff doc that maps which percentiles/ windows each side owns.
ajay: test plan: run a chaos test where operator requests bursts (10x) and central occasionally denies 50% to verify graceful degradation and no request loss. record histograms at 10s resolution.
sophie: UX: add a visualization in console showing active intents/grants per-pool and a time-series of granted_prewarms vs usage to help debugging.
dave: open question — should operator be allowed to proactively request node-month scale (long-lived) or only short-lived prewarms? leaning short-lived only; long-lived should be central's domain.
kevin: action items: 1) I'll draft a tiny RFC for ScaleIntent contract + lease lifecycle. 2) maria/ajay to propose sampling/aggregation format for telemetry. 3) sophie to sketch console UI for intents. 4) dave to design chaos test. I'll add these to the RFC checklist.
sophie: can we add a quick fallback policy: if operator keeps getting <requested_prewarms for N attempts, escalate to central as "sustained pressure" so central can provision capacity?
kevin: yes — escalate threshold as part of the contract (e.g., escalate_after_attempts=3). add an explicit tag so we can metricize.
ajay: one more: prefer to send intent over gRPC with streaming replies so grants can be updated quickly. but fall back to HTTP for private deployments.
maria: ok, looks actionable. small note: mind PCI/regulatory clusters — telemetry payload must be scrubbed/PII-free.
dave: +1. I'll start a repo with a mock operator and central stub to iterate on the contract.
kevin: great. I'll post the RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. thanks all :rocket:
